input.rationale: Interpreted the healing-phase successor receipt and recorded the durable fact it establishes. Receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 parsed four events and evaluated all ten comparisons: the carried-over seven behave exactly as in the previous run (five violated witnesses at indices 1 and 2, two controls holding), and the two new healed-phase assertions are violated at event index 3 - the nodes still hold different payloads at the conflict index with the same term (A and C minority-write against B, D and E majority-write, all term 3), and the restarted node still reports {A,B,C} after the cluster is whole again and committing, with its log advancing to index 12 as the progress control confirms. The child question's third limitation (post-healing fate of the conflicting entry) is therefore resolved, the parent's persistence limitation narrows to long-run persistence, and the AppendEntries reconciliation behaviour behind the permanent divergence is recorded as reusable knowledge. Also filed an experiment for the other registered question in this feature: a harness that builds a snapshot at index 1000 plus 9000 committed LogCommand entries above it and constructs the node in both modes. Local construction feedback showed the first fixture attempt with LogNoop entries returned immediately because prepareLog never sends no-ops to the FSM, so the entries were changed to the commit path; the feature-on case then failed to return within the 5s window while the identical fixture with the feature off returned with lastApplied still at the snapshot index, which isolates the replay as the cause.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and no snapshot install.

interpretations.rationale: This revision reproduces the split-brain window and adds the healing phase; every assertion is contradicted or confirmed as predicted. Admission index 0 again establishes snapshot index 6 with {A,B,C}, the committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E} and a stored commit index of 8 covering it. After the restart (index 1) the node reports {A,B,C}. In the split (index 2) A leads the two-voter partition while D leads the other three, so leader_count is 2, both leaders commit at index 11 in term 3 with different payloads, and the minority leader's write commits, while the in-partition control C never leads and the majority keeps reporting {A,B,C,D,E} (comparisons 5 and 6 hold). New in this revision, after the partition is healed, one further entry is committed and the cluster is whole (index 3): the payloads at index 11 remain different on different nodes with the same term 3 (A,C minority-write against B,D,E majority-write), so the entries cannot be reconciled by term comparison (comparison 7 violated), and the restarted node's own view is still {A,B,C} although its log advanced to index 12 and the current leader reports {A,B,C,D,E} (comparison 8 violated, comparison 9 holds as the progress control). Comparison-level basis for the persistence is knowledge @same_term_divergence_unrepairable for the entry divergence and the duplicate-skip behaviour for the configuration: the leader never re-sends the committed configuration entry to a log that already stores it, and a same-term duplicate is skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry. Limits: the healed sample is one window after a single further entry, in-memory stores, a graceful shutdown instead of a crash and a transport-only partition; the healed leader varied across runs (in this receipt D; local repeats produced A once and D or E otherwise), so the receipt does not claim that the stale node leads a healed cluster; and whether a snapshot install or log compaction eventually repairs the divergent entries is unobserved.
counterevidence: In this receipt the healed cluster elected D, a node with the current configuration, so the stale node does not always lead once the partition is removed.
The progress control holds: the restarted node's log advanced after healing, so the stale view is not a symptom of a stalled or isolated node.
limitations: The healed observation is a single sample after one further committed entry; no long run, no further membership change and no snapshot install is covered.
The healed leader identity varies between runs, so nothing is concluded about which node leads after healing.
In-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown of the restarted node rather than a crash.

interpretations.rationale: Answer, now with the post-split phase observed: yes. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay wins an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log while the remaining voters elect their own leader, and the damage outlives the partition. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e gives the split window (A leading two voters, D or B leading three, both committing at index 11 in term 3), and receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 repeats that window and then heals it, showing that after a further committed entry the five nodes still disagree about the payload at index 11 while agreeing on its term, and that the restarted node still uses {A,B,C} although its log advanced to index 12 and the serving leader knows {A,B,C,D,E}. The restarted node's log advances normally, so nothing about its participation or connectivity explains the stale view.
limitations: One cluster per run with a single partition window and a single healed sample.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft never rebuilds the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum; that stale view lets it lead with two votes where the current configuration requires three, produces two concurrent leaders with conflicting commits at the same index and term, and the stale view survives the partition being healed while the node keeps participating. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed configuration entry, which is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry; quorum and voter admission come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096, 1660-1680); duplicates are skipped so no later AppendEntries reprocesses the entry (raft.go 1526-1553); and the persisted commit index exists only because the node ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Witnesses: receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 for the configuration and quorum state on supplied stores (feature on: {A,B,C}, quorum 2; feature off: {A,B,C,D,E}, quorum 3), receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e for the split (A leads two voters, three others elect their own leader, conflicting commits at index 11 term 3, minority commit accepted), and receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 for the healed state (divergent payloads at index 11 with equal terms remain, the restarted node stays at {A,B,C} while its log advances to 12). investigations.question: When Config.RestoreCommittedLogs replays committed logs during NewRaft, which configuration does the restarted node end up using for candidate admission and election quorum if its last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry that its own log already contains?
investigations.hypothesis: The eager replay moves lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the configuration scan, so the scan starts above the committed configuration entry; r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed remain the snapshot's configuration, and the node derives quorumSize/hasVote from that older membership until some later configuration entry is appended.
investigations.discriminator: Same restart-shaped stores (snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log index 6 = committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, persisted commit index 7) constructed twice: RestoreCommittedLogs=false (control) vs true. Predicted difference: lastApplied 5 vs 7, latest config index 6 ({A,B,C,D,E}) vs 1 ({A,B,C}), quorumSize 3 vs 2. A third case runs the feature-on fixture without skipStartup and samples the node's public GetConfiguration while it is campaigning.

investigations.question: Can NewRaft fail to return when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs replays more committed log entries than processLogs can enqueue on fsmMutateCh before runFSM is started?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs runs before goFunc(r.runFSM); processLogs blocks once fsmMutateCh (buffered 128) is full, and each batch holds up to MaxAppendEntries entries, so a replay of more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries leaves the constructor waiting for a consumer that does not exist yet.
investigations.discriminator: Construct a node whose CommitTrackingLogStore reports a commit index at least 128*MaxAppendEntries+1 entries above the snapshot/applied index and observe whether NewRaft returns, with the batch-consumer set (runFSM started or not) as the changing condition.

investigations.question: Can a node whose configuration was left stale by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay actually win an election with fewer votes than a majority of the configuration recorded in its own committed log, while the remaining voters elect their own leader?
investigations.hypothesis: With the restarted node holding {A,B,C} while its log records the committed {A,B,C,D,E}, isolating it with one voter of the stale set lets it collect two votes (itself plus that voter) against its stale quorum of two and become leader, while the three remaining voters, who hold the current configuration, elect a second leader; both then accept commands.
investigations.discriminator: One cluster whose only difference is the defect: node A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change beyond its snapshot, then a partition separates A and one stale voter from the other three. Predicted difference against a control restart of the same node without RestoreCommittedLogs (or with a refreshed snapshot): the feature-on node reaches Leader with two votes; the control stays follower/candidate because its quorum is three.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft's post-restore configuration scan iterates index from max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 up to the last log index and calls processConfigurationLogEntry for every entry in that range, so configuration entries at or below the scan start are never processed into r.configurations during construction.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a Raft instance from retained log/stable/snapshot state; the scan runs after restoreSnapshot and after restoreFromCommittedLogs, and before skipStartup returns control to the caller.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets the in-memory commit index from store.GetCommitIndex() (clamped to the log's last index) and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs enqueues the corresponding commitTuples on fsmMutateCh and then sets lastApplied to that index.
knowledge.conditions: Called during NewRaft, after snapshot restore and before runFSM is started; the log store must implement CommitTrackingLogStore or NewRaft returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore.

knowledge.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.
knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.

Admission index 0 establishes the setup: snapshot index 6 with configuration {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8 covering that entry, and A reporting the five-voter membership before the restart. result.summary: Interpreted the healing-phase successor receipt and opened the other registered question with a filed experiment. Receipt 455e647ad0794a16903414b5a8846276 parsed four events and evaluated all ten comparisons: the carried seven reproduce the split-brain window (violated at indices 1 and 2, controls holding), and both new healed-phase assertions are violated at event index 3 — the nodes still hold different payloads at conflict index 11 with the same term 3 (A and C minority-write against B, D and E majority-write), and the restarted node still reports {A,B,C} after the cluster is whole and committing, with its log advancing to 12 as the progress control. That resolves the child question's post-healing limitation; its disposition is now explained and its rationale, the parent account and the joint history across the three receipts were rewritten, with the parent's persistence limitation narrowed to long-run/repair-path coverage and the healed-leader variance recorded as counterevidence. A new fact records why such same-term divergence is never reconciled by AppendEntries (truncation needs a term difference; same-term duplicates are skipped). Finally, I filed an experiment for the registered constructor question: one node with a snapshot at index 1000 and 9000 committed LogCommand entries staged as commit index 10000, constructed with the feature off and on, which locally showed the feature-off control returning with lastApplied still at 1000 while the feature-on constructor never returned within the 5s window — the first fixture attempt with LogNoop entries returned in both modes, which is why the entries were moved to the commit path. Incomplete: that experiment's receipt and interpretation, the no-feature restart control inside the cluster, and whether a snapshot install or compaction eventually repairs the divergent entries.

investigations.question: When Config.RestoreCommittedLogs replays committed logs during NewRaft, which configuration does the restarted node end up using for candidate admission and election quorum if its last snapshot predates a committed configuration entry that its own log already contains?
investigations.hypothesis: The eager replay moves lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the configuration scan, so the scan starts above the committed configuration entry; r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed remain the snapshot's configuration, and the node derives quorumSize/hasVote from that older membership until some later configuration entry is appended.
investigations.discriminator: Same restart-shaped stores (snapshot index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log index 6 = committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, persisted commit index 7) constructed twice: RestoreCommittedLogs=false (control) vs true. Predicted difference: lastApplied 5 vs 7, latest config index 6 ({A,B,C,D,E}) vs 1 ({A,B,C}), quorumSize 3 vs 2. A third case runs the feature-on fixture without skipStartup and samples the node's public GetConfiguration while it is campaigning.

investigations.question: Can NewRaft fail to return when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs replays more committed log entries than processLogs can enqueue on fsmMutateCh before runFSM is started?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs runs before goFunc(r.runFSM); processLogs blocks once fsmMutateCh (buffered 128) is full, and each batch holds up to MaxAppendEntries entries, so a replay of more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries leaves the constructor waiting for a consumer that does not exist yet.
investigations.discriminator: Construct a node whose CommitTrackingLogStore reports a commit index at least 128*MaxAppendEntries+1 entries above the snapshot/applied index and observe whether NewRaft returns, with the batch-consumer set (runFSM started or not) as the changing condition.

investigations.question: Can a node whose configuration was left stale by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay actually win an election with fewer votes than a majority of the configuration recorded in its own committed log, while the remaining voters elect their own leader?
investigations.hypothesis: With the restarted node holding {A,B,C} while its log records the committed {A,B,C,D,E}, isolating it with one voter of the stale set lets it collect two votes (itself plus that voter) against its stale quorum of two and become leader, while the three remaining voters, who hold the current configuration, elect a second leader; both then accept commands.
investigations.discriminator: One cluster whose only difference is the defect: node A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a committed configuration change beyond its snapshot, then a partition separates A and one stale voter from the other three. Predicted difference against a control restart of the same node without RestoreCommittedLogs (or with a refreshed snapshot): the feature-on node reaches Leader with two votes; the control stays follower/candidate because its quorum is three.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft's post-restore configuration scan iterates index from max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 up to the last log index and calls processConfigurationLogEntry for every entry in that range, so configuration entries at or below the scan start are never processed into r.configurations during construction.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a Raft instance from retained log/stable/snapshot state; the scan runs after restoreSnapshot and after restoreFromCommittedLogs, and before skipStartup returns control to the caller.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets the in-memory commit index from store.GetCommitIndex() (clamped to the log's last index) and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs enqueues the corresponding commitTuples on fsmMutateCh and then sets lastApplied to that index.
knowledge.conditions: Called during NewRaft, after snapshot restore and before runFSM is started; the log store must implement CommitTrackingLogStore or NewRaft returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore.

knowledge.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.
knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

knowledge.statement: Two entries that end up at the same log index with the same term but different payloads on different servers are never reconciled by AppendEntries: the receiver truncates its suffix only when an incoming entry at an existing index has a different term, and an entry whose index and term match the stored one is skipped as a duplicate before any configuration or log processing, so the divergence persists while the cluster continues to commit later entries.
knowledge.conditions: AppendEntries conflict handling (raft.go 1526-1553) on a follower whose stored entry at that index has the same term; observed after the split-leader window of the RestoreCommittedLogs restart defect was healed with a further committed entry and no snapshot install.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

The feature's documented purpose (config.go 243-255) is to replay committed logs into the FSM, so changing the scan start index may have been intentional; the account rests on the resulting membership state, not on the intent.
limitations: The experiment supplies the durable state (snapshot at index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log entry 6 = LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, StageCommitIndex(7)) rather than producing it with a live cluster, so the fixture asserts reachability by source reasoning rather than by an executed prefix.
